newsitem.title: USA: Fed expected to add reserves via overnight systems.
newsitem.headline: Fed expected to add reserves via overnight systems.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is expected to add temporary reserves to the banking system on Wednesday, analysts said.
"We expect overnight systems," said Lee Youngdahl, bond market analyst at Aubrey G. Lanston, citing a residual add need at the end of the two-week bank reserve maintenance period.
Forecasts for an overnight system repurchase operation were ubiquitous.
Analysts at the advisory firms of I.D.E.A. and MMS International said they expected it, as did Kevin Flanagan, first vice president and money market economist at Dean Witter Reynolds Inc.
At 0947 EST/1447 GMT, Federal funds traded at 5-5/16 percent, above the Fed's 5-1/4 percent target for the rate.
Analysts have also said that the Fed could add permanent reserves to the banking system through a coupon pass as early as Friday.
(( -- Ellen Freilich, North American Treasury Desk 212-859-1679))
